text:
alex: seeing a wild spike in us-west-2 gpu node churn, nodepool-gpu-3 is bouncing between Provisioning -> NotReady -> Terminated. Pods pile up in Pending. Anyone oncall? :rotating_light:

maria: oncall here. can you paste the CA events/logs? suspecting spot preemptions + k8s scale loop.

sam: paste of `kubectl get nodes -o wide` shows ~18 nodes NotReady, a bunch with taint `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoExecute` and many showing `ProviderID: aws:///.../i-xxxxx (terminated)`. also seeing a lot of `ErrImagePull` on a few pods but mostly Pending for scheduling.

autoscaler-bot: [alert] cluster-autoscaler: Launching 40 nodes for nodepool-gpu-3 (scale up) -> scaling activity started. recent scale down events: 30 nodes removed in last 7m.

dave: this looks like a classic thundering-surge: cronjobs + batch jobs all restarted and CA scaled up, then spot churn kills them and CA scales down — repeat. we should throttle CA and pause any non-critical cronjobs.

irene: i'm seeing a runaway scheduled job: `daily-embeddings-janitor` started 500 parallel workers after a missed window. can we suspend it?

oncall-rotation: suspending cronjob `daily-embeddings-janitor` now -> `kubectl patch cronjob daily-embeddings-janitor -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'` :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks. temporary mitigation idea: 1) set nodepool-gpu-3 max to +50 nodes (force capacity), 2) set `--scale-down-delay-after-add` to 10m on CA, 3) mark nodepool as mixed on-demand for now. any objections? cost will spike.

maria: agree on delay change and suspend jobs. can you run the CA flag change as a hotfix? we can also add an annotation to the problematic deployments: `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false"` only for stateful/in-flight ones.

sam: running commands now:```
# increase max for nodepool-gpu-3
aws eks update-nodegroup-config --cluster-name prod --nodegroup-name nodepool-gpu-3 --scaling-config minSize=10,maxSize=120,desiredSize=30
# patch CA deployment args
kubectl -n kube-system set args deployment/cluster-autoscaler -- --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m
```

autoscaler-bot: [info] scale-up request submitted. AWS ASG activity started. note: spot capacity fluctuating in us-west-2-azb.

dave: also recommend setting a short-lived kill switch: annotate the heavy cron/deployments with `redwood/inference-emergency-reduce-parallelism: "true"` and roll a quick patch to reduce replicas / concurrency. that'll lower pressure without full rollback.

irene: applying replica dampening to `inference-batcher` and `embed-worker` now: `kubectl scale deployment inference-batcher --replicas=2` and `kubectl patch deploy embed-worker -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"embed-worker","env":[{"name":"MAX_PARALLEL","value":"4"}]}]}}}}'`

alex: OK, CA is stabilizing but we see a backlog in queue. i'll open a quick runbook note: we may need to convert a couple of spot subgroups to on-demand for the next 24h. cost ops FYI.

oncall-rotation: digging into cloud console, converting 2 ASGs from spot->on-demand fallback (hotfix) — this will take ~6-8m to warm.

maria: thanks. postmortem items to track: - tighten cron concurrency defaults, - add CA floor for gpu pools, - automated detection to temporarily pause mass-cron restarts, - cost runbook for emergency on-demand conversion.

dave: agreed. also let's add a circuit breaker to our job-scheduler to reject >X parallel tasks when pool utilization >80%.

alex: wrapping up: everything is improving, node churn dropped after on-demand fallback. keeping cronjobs suspended and replicas reduced for 30m. will follow up with a short incident note. :thumbsup:

sam: saving logs/snippets to `s3://redwood-incident-logs/2218765432/` and creating a PR to add CA conservative flags.

autoscaler-bot: [resolved] cluster-autoscaler: activity normalized, scale up/down rate back to baseline.

irene: re-enabling `daily-embeddings-janitor` in 30m once capacity stable.

alex: thanks team — incident contained.
